# Troubleshooting {#admin-troubleshooting}

## Listing and diagnosing the system

- `kailash list` — the CLI's manifest-baked listing of installed
  categories and tools. Because the listing is baked from the
  manifest at build time (the drift-killer design), what it shows is
  what the system declaration carries — compare it against your
  enabled categories when diagnosing a "missing tool" report.
- `kailash manifest validate` (via the packages flake, as the release
  checklist runs it) — checks a manifest against the schema;
  validators' output is the first thing a release review records.

## Common situations

- **Boot/imaging**: verify the checksum against the release's
  SHA256SUMS sheet first; size-budget overruns indicate a stray
  opt-in data derivation enabled on an image that excludes it —
  heavy packs ride `kailash-data.*` toggles, off on default images.
- **Rebuild against a moved lock**: a tool failing after a lock pull
  is a pin that moved — check the pin's derivation and the bump PR's
  smoke evidence before rolling the lock back; report defects with
  the release tag on the repository tracker.
- **Category smoke failures**: per-category VM smoke tests gate CI;
  a failing smoke names the category module to look at first.

## Reporting defects

Track findings on the project's GitHub issue trackers with the
release tag in the report — findings do not live only in local
notes. The guide's own defects (broken links, stale pages) are
reported on the kailash-guide repository.
